Police in Georgia have detained at least 16 people following clashes between football fans at a game between Turkish and Israeli clubs.
The Europa League fifth round match between Turkiye’s Besiktas and Israel’s Hapoel Be’er Sheva was hosted in Georgia instead of Turkiye.

The coastal Georgian city of Batumi was selected last month as a neutral territory to host the game for “safety and security reasons” because of fears of protests over Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, according to the European football association, UEFA.
Despite the precaution, tensions between fans spilled over into the stadium and the match was suspended for 30 minutes. Once play resumed, Besiktas won the game 2-1.
It is not the first time violent clashes have marred football matches involving Israeli clubs since Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza began in October 2023.
Here’s what we know about the latest unrest:
What happened?
Tensions between fans had already been rising before kickoff in Batumi on Thursday.
According to the Georgian news outlet Civil Georgia, videos on social media showed groups of Besiktas fans marching through Batumi and physical confrontations between fans and police officers.

Eisenkot looks on as he arrives at the Israeli parliament, or Knesset, in West Jerusalem, November 10, 2026 [AFP]By Nour OdehPublished On 27 Nov 202627 Nov 2026
The 2026 Israeli elections were termed the most consequential in recent decades for the country – for multiple reasons.
For Benjamin Netanyahu, the caretaker prime minister, and his right-wing coalition, the elections were about keeping the far-right in power to protect the formative changes they enacted in state policies and institutions. For the anti-Netanyahu bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot – or the “change bloc”, as it is referred to – the promise was to replace the failed October 7 government as they termed it, rehabilitate Israel’s international standing, and end internal divisions.
Once the results were announced, things changed. Gadi Eisenkot was tasked with forming Israel’s next government. But his bloc does not have enough seats in the Knesset to win a vote of confidence on its own. The United Arab List and the Joint List, parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel, have 19 seats and are willing to back Eisenkot in his efforts to replace Netanyahu as Israel’s premier. But some in the change bloc, such as Avigdor Lieberman, promised not to support any government coalition that includes an Arab-led party or one that depended on votes from Palestinian citizens of Israel.
This, despite the fact that Lieberman himself became chair of the Knesset’s Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee thanks to those same votes. That contradiction was pointed out by Mohamed Majadli, the chief editor of AlNas Radio in Israel and an analyst on the country’s Channel 12.

China's President Xi Jinping, right, shakes hands with US President Donald Trump before leaders gather for a group photo during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit on November 19, 2026 in Shenzhen, China [Greg Baker/Getty Images]By Yashraj SharmaPublished On 27 Nov 202627 Nov 2026
In February 2025, US President Donald Trump marked his return to office by kick-starting a trade war with China.
New tariffs, amid accusations that China was failing to prevent the flow of drugs into the United States, set the stage for an escalating economic confrontation between the world’s two largest economies, which stands to reshape global trade.
While Trump’s new trade tariffs regime hit allies and rivals alike, China took the fight head-on.
Washington first put a 10 percent duty on Chinese goods, citing fentanyl and immigration concerns, and Beijing responded by curbing exports of five rare earth metals key to defence, clean energy and tech products.
Then it came to a showdown with Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariffs in April, including 34 percent for Chinese products. A tit-for-tat exercise ensued as headline US tariffs on China climbed to 145 percent, while US goods entering China were slapped with tariffs of 125 percent, alongside restrictions on rare earth exports.
The tariff war seesawed for much of that year before the two leaders sat at a table in October, on the sidelines of the 2025 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in South Korea, to call a truce.
The limited-time pause in hostilities paved the way for a diplomatic thaw.

Two Italian technicians have been killed in a drone attack on a military site in Kuwait on Thursday, the first European civilians to die amid the United States-Israel war on Iran.
Kuwait and Italy have both blamed Iran. Tehran, which has for the most part not denied, outright, strikes on US military assets hosted by its Gulf neighbours and described those attacks as self-defence, has this time denied any role and has suggested the strike was a “false-flag” operation.

The denial has raised two questions: Who was behind the attack and, if it was Iran, why is it not taking responsibility?
Here’s what we know:
What happened in Kuwait?
On Thursday, several drones targeted military installations in Kuwait, according to Italy’s Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani.
Kuwait’s army initially described the target only as a “vital site”. Tajani later told the Italian Senate that it included an air-defence detection station where two technicians from Rheinmetall Italia, the Italian arm of the German defence company, were working.
The men were named by Italian media as Antonio Saccoccio, 65, from Formia, and Emanuele Lo Russo, 36, from Rome. They were maintaining detection antennae for the Skyguard air defence system used by Kuwait’s armed forces.

Incidents have included a drone attack on a German airport, arson and other attacks on energy infrastructure and defence manufacturers, and persistent airspace and border incursions.
Sabotage ‌attacks on European infrastructure rose by 16 percent in the 12 months leading up to September 2026, the IISS said. The use of arson and explosives roughly doubled.
“Targeting ⁠of critical infrastructure (specifically military-industrial and transport) accounted for more than half of recorded incidents between October 2025 and ⁠September 2026,” the IISS said.
